terra.problem: “Easy to grab the wrong one” uses “wrong” about the baker’s answer.
The caravan line jokes about the LORD as company who does not need a ride. Humor must not target God.
The passage says Joseph was put in charge of Potiphar’s household; it does not establish that no soldiers were under his care.
The explanation is flat and repetitive: it says three times that the verse speaks of blessing rather than warning, without adding insight.
The joke about lifting a lid on a batch too soon has no clear connection to Potiphar concerning himself with his food.
“The one thing he can’t touch” turns Joseph’s refusal of Potiphar’s wife into a restriction on touching that the text does not give.
“He’s looking at God when he says it” adds an action the text does not give. Joseph is speaking to Potiphar’s wife.
“He stayed out of her reach” overstates Joseph’s refusal to be near her. She later grabs him by his cloak.
No household servant was inside, but that does not mean there was nobody to call. Potiphar’s wife subsequently calls the servants.
The explanation is generic and merely repeats that the named feeling is anger, without adding context or insight.
“Not yet” implies Joseph will later walk free, giving away what happens next in the story.
